title: Apple Crumble
subtitle: Spiced apple filling under a buttery oat crumble
excerpt: Peeled apples cooked with sugar and cinnamon, covered with a buttery crumble of flour, oats, and butter, then baked until the topping is golden and crisp and the apple bubbles through. Britain's favourite pudding.

recipe.sourceNotes: Crumble was developed in Britain during the Second World War as a less ingredient-intensive alternative to pastry when rationing made butter and flour scarce. Rubbed fat, flour, and sugar give a sandy, rubble-like topping that bakes to a satisfying crunch. The inclusion of oats, which became popular in the postwar period, gives a heartier topping. Apple is the classic filling but rhubarb, blackberry, pear, and plum are all traditional. Serve with custard, cream, or vanilla ice cream.

content.text: The butter for the crumble must be cold: if it is too warm it will blend completely into the flour rather than forming the rubble-like lumps that give the topping its texture. Keep the pieces of butter uneven rather than rubbing them in too thoroughly. The crumble is done when the top is golden and the apple filling is bubbling up through the sides.

items.preparation: cooking apples, peeled, cored, and sliced

content.text: Heat the oven to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. Toss the apple slices with the caster sugar and cinnamon. Arrange in an oven-proof dish.
Rub the cold butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs with some larger lumps remaining. Stir in the oats and soft brown sugar.

Spread the crumble topping evenly over the apple. Do not press it down. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the topping is golden and the apple is tender when pierced with a knife. Serve with custard, cream, or vanilla ice cream.
